core_obligations: Chain of bijections (proof lines 2818-2831): for an arbitrary sheaf the author computes the morphism set out of the sheafification of the left Kan extension of the sheafified presheaf and rewrites it successively by the adjunction with the direct image, by the identification of morphisms into the direct image with morphisms of presheaves, by the universal property of sheafification, and by the adjunction defining the left Kan extension, obtaining the morphism set out of the sheafification of the left Kan extension of the original presheaf.
Conclusion (proof line 2832): the two sheaves represent the same functor on sheaves, so they agree by the Yoneda lemma.
proof_roadmap: Compare the functors represented by the two sheaves on an arbitrary sheaf.
Rewrite the morphism sets using the two adjunctions and the universal property of sheafification.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that sheafifying the left Kan extension of a presheaf gives the same sheaf as sheafifying the left Kan extension of its sheafification (statement lines 2810-2815). The proof is a complete computation: the author compares the functors represented by the two sheaves and rewrites the morphism sets through the adjunction with the direct image, the identification of morphisms into a direct image with morphisms of presheaves, the universal property of sheafification and the adjunction defining the left Kan extension (proof lines 2818-2831), concluding by the Yoneda lemma (proof line 2832). The non-formal content is the chain of adjunction rewritings. The claim is H1: a written-out computation with each input named.
